Maya C: quick q — for the quieting rollout RFC, are we leaning into a per-tenant tier (gold/silver/bronze) that maps to preset quiet-windows + scaled thresholds?
Jordan P: yes, that was the sketch. gold => short window, stricter false-positive tolerance; bronze => longer quiet window, higher signal aggregation before notify :thinking_face:
Owen L: main API implication: we need a route that returns effective notify-policy for a tenant at eval-time. something like `GET /v1/tenants/:id/notify-policy?time=...` so console + runtime can show exact behavior
Maya C: that endpoint should also return the computed SLO exposure & debt burn rate used to trigger the policy. UX needs a single number in the card, not 5 nested fields.
Sam R: telemetry question — do we want token-level cost breakdown included when we show alert context? ops asked for per-route spend next to SLO alert to justify paging
Jordan P: agreed, but that's heavy. maybe only attach a pre-computed cost-estimate snapshot (last 1h) to reduce cardinality. metadata-> {cost_est, last_window}
Owen L: implementation note: if runtime evaluates policy with fallback (tier->fallback-route->soft-snooze), console must show the chain and last applied reason. otherwise product teams confused.
Maya C: UX idea — in the SLO card, show: current_exposure, effective_threshold, notify_window, last_fired(reason). small inline help with hover explaining tier defaults and how overrides apply.
Sam R: can we expose the override API? product wants button in console: "Temporarily reduce notify sensitivity" that calls `POST /v1/tenants/:id/notify-overrides` with TTL
Jordan P: we need guardrails. allow TTL <= 6h for non-admins, admins can do up to 7d. also logable and auditable (KMS/HSM trace we already have for private customers)
Maya C: rollout plan proposal: stage 1 — surface computed policy in console (read-only). stage 2 — add soft overrides for dev tenants. stage 3 — expose POST for prod with admin gate + audit logs
Owen L: API debate: should console compute effective policy client-side (fetch base + overrides) or rely on server to return single canonical policy? leaning server-side to avoid client mismatch.
Jordan P: server-side makes rollbacks simpler and a single source of truth. + easier to add runtime feature flags for gradual rollout.
Sam R: testing — I'll prod a canary that fires a synthetic SLO breach for a sandbox tenant to validate quieting chain. canary should create a fake signal and check `last_applied_reason` is "quota-backpressure" or similar
alert-bot: test-alert — synthetic SLO breach for tenant sandbox-42 registered at 3241598800 :bell: (no page)  
Maya C: perfect, that confirms webhook + console updates. thanks all — I'll write the staged rollout ticket and link the API contract mockups.
Jordan P: assign to eng-runtime + eng-platform, label `slo-quiet-tiering` and add ETA 2 sprints? :+1:
Owen L: will add API PR with contract and small sample responses. planning to return both `computed_policy` and `explain_chain` to keep console simple.
Sam R: leaving notes for QA: validate cost snapshot accuracy and ensure no PII in alert context. QA checklist in the ticket.
Maya C: sweet. next sync Thursday standup to sign off on stage1 docs.
